scenario: 模型整体指标很好就要上线，但你担心某些子群体被平均值盖住了。
scenario_en: The model's overall metric looks great and you're about to ship, but you worry some subgroups are hidden by the average.
q: slice-based evaluation 是什么？它比看 aggregate 指标多做了什么？
q_en: What is slice-based evaluation, and what does it add over aggregate metrics?
why: 切片评估 = 定义有意义的子集（slice）、逐 slice 算指标、把每个 slice 的阈值当上线闸门。它把「一个数」拆成「一张矩阵」，让少数群体的退化不再被多数群体的高分数学上淹没。
why_en: Slice-based evaluation defines meaningful subsets, computes metrics per slice, and enforces per-slice thresholds as release gates, turning one number into a matrix.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["eval set"] --> S["slicing functions
切成子集"] S --> M["逐 slice 算指标
输出矩阵"] M --> G["per-slice 阈值
上线闸门"]
options: 只把 aggregate 指标算得更精确一点，用更大的验证集降低方差
定义有意义的子集、逐 slice 算指标、把每个 slice 的阈值当上线闸门，输出是矩阵不是一个数
把所有子群合并成一个更大的均值，让指标更稳定好看
只在出问题后再去看哪个子群差，是一种事后调试手段
options_en: Just compute the aggregate metric more precisely with a larger validation set to cut variance.
Define meaningful subsets, compute metrics per slice, and enforce per-slice thresholds as release gates — output is a matrix, not one number.
Merge all subgroups into a bigger average so the metric looks more stable.
Only look at which subgroup is bad after something breaks — a post-hoc debugging move.
optionExplanations: 更大验证集只让均值更准，还是一个数，照样盖住少数群体的退化。
对；切片把一个数拆成矩阵，并把 per-slice 阈值升级成可阻断上线的闸门，这是它的核心。
合并成更大均值方向反了——正是均值淹没少数群体，切片要做的是拆开而不是合并。
切片是主动的发布前门禁，不是出事后才用的事后调试；它把子群体验收前置。
optionExplanations_en: A larger validation set only sharpens the average — still one number that hides subgroup degradation.
Correct — slicing turns one number into a matrix and upgrades per-slice thresholds into release-blocking gates, its core idea.
Merging into a bigger average is backwards — averaging is what drowns minorities; slicing splits rather than merges.
Slicing is a proactive pre-release gate, not post-hoc debugging; it front-loads subgroup acceptance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某维度（地区/设备/用户类型）划出的评估子集，用来单独考核该子群。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slice is an evaluation subset defined by a dimension (region/device/user-type) to grade that subgroup on its own.

scenario: Airbnb 搜索报告 NDCG@10 = 0.78 就准备上线，但 80% 的评估流量来自北美/欧洲，东南亚房源的 NDCG@10 只有 0.51。
scenario_en: Airbnb search reports NDCG@10 = 0.78 and is ready to ship, but 80% of eval traffic is NA/EU, while SE Asia listings sit at NDCG@10 = 0.51.
q: 这个 0.78 与 0.51 的对比说明了什么设计问题？
q_en: What design problem does the 0.78 vs 0.51 gap reveal?
why: 0.78 是按流量加权的均值：80% 的 NA/EU 高分「数学上淹没」了东南亚的 0.51，退化在总数里看不见。含义是必须逐 slice 看指标——地区就是一个必须单列的 slice，否则会带着 0.51 的体验上线。
why_en: The 0.78 is traffic-weighted, so 80% NA/EU mathematically drowns SE Asia's 0.51, meaning you must evaluate per slice or ship a 0.51 experience unseen.
options: 东南亚房源太少，可以忽略，0.78 已经代表了整体质量
加权均值让 80% 的 NA/EU 高分淹没东南亚的 0.51，退化被隐藏——必须逐 slice（如地区）单独验收
0.51 只是噪声，样本一多自然会回到 0.78 附近
说明 NDCG 这个指标本身失效了，应该换成 precision
options_en: SE Asia listings are too few to matter; 0.78 already represents overall quality.
The weighted average lets 80% NA/EU drown SE Asia's 0.51, hiding the degradation — you must grade per slice (e.g. region).
The 0.51 is just noise that will drift back toward 0.78 as samples grow.
It shows NDCG itself is broken and should be replaced with precision.
optionExplanations: 『太少可忽略』正是失败心态：那是一个真实市场的糟糕体验，均值掩盖不等于问题不存在。
对；这正是均值淹没少数群体的教科书案例，结论是把地区当强制 slice 单列验收。
0.51 vs 0.78 是系统性差距不是噪声，靠加样本回不到 0.78，反而要专门处理东南亚这个 slice。
NDCG 没失效——失效的是只看它的 aggregate；同一个 NDCG 逐 slice 算就暴露了问题。
optionExplanations_en: 'Too few to matter' is the failure mindset: that's a real market's poor experience, and a hidden average doesn't make it go away.
Correct — a textbook case of the average drowning a minority; the takeaway is to grade region as a mandatory slice.
0.51 vs 0.78 is a systematic gap, not noise; more samples won't lift it to 0.78 — SE Asia needs dedicated handling.
NDCG isn't broken — looking only at its aggregate is; the same NDCG computed per slice exposes the problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序质量指标：看前 10 个结果的相关性并按位置折扣，归一化到 0-1，越高越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG@10 (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at 10) rates the top-10 results' relevance with position discounting, normalized to 0-1.

scenario: 要把评估集切成子群，团队讨论用什么形式定义这些切分规则。
scenario_en: To split the eval set into subgroups, the team debates how to define the partition rules.
q: slicing function 是什么形态，为什么这样设计？
q_en: What form does a slicing function take, and why?
why: slicing function 就像 SQL 的 WHERE 子句，把评估集切成子群，例如 is_new_user(x) = account_age < 7 days。写成代码函数是为了简单、可测试、能和模型代码一起版本化，slice 定义随代码演进而受审。
why_en: A slicing function is like a SQL WHERE clause partitioning the eval set, written as code so it's simple, testable, and version-controlled alongside the model.
options: 一份人工维护的 Excel 名单，列出属于每个子群的样本 id
像 SQL WHERE 子句的代码函数（如 account_age < 7），简单、可测试、与模型代码一起版本化
一个训练好的分类模型，用来预测样本属于哪个 slice
一次性的临时查询，分析完就丢，不进代码库
options_en: A hand-maintained spreadsheet listing which sample ids belong to each subgroup.
A code function like a SQL WHERE clause (e.g. account_age < 7), simple, testable, and version-controlled with the model code.
A trained classifier that predicts which slice a sample belongs to.
A one-off ad-hoc query thrown away after analysis, never committed.
optionExplanations: 人工名单不可测试、不可复现，样本一变就失效，无法当发布门禁的稳定依据。
对；代码化的 WHERE 谓词可单测、可版本化，slice 定义就能随人群演进被 review 和迭代。
用模型预测 slice 会引入第二个模型的误差和不可解释性，切分应是确定性的谓词。
一次性临时查询无法进 CI/CD 当门禁，切分必须持久化、和模型代码同生命周期。
optionExplanations_en: A hand list isn't testable or reproducible and breaks when samples change — no stable basis for a release gate.
Correct — a coded WHERE predicate is unit-testable and version-controlled, so slice definitions can be reviewed and evolved with the population.
Predicting the slice with a model injects a second model's error and opacity; partitioning should be a deterministic predicate.
A one-off query can't become a CI/CD gate; partitions must be persisted and share the model's lifecycle.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个把评估样本判为属于/不属于某子群的布尔谓词，形如 SQL WHERE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slicing function is a boolean predicate deciding whether an eval sample belongs to a subgroup, like a SQL WHERE clause.

scenario: 要建一套 slice 目录，讨论这些 slice 该从哪里来。
scenario_en: Building a slice catalog, you discuss where the slices should come from.
q: 文中给出的 slice 三个来源是哪些？(多选)
q_en: What are the three sources of slices in the lesson? (multiple)
why: 三来源：① 业务关键 segment（利益相关者点名的高价值群体，如付费订阅/高 LTV）→ 强制 slice；② 错误分析驱动（历史失败模式转成 slicing function）；③ 算法自动发现（如在误差残差上拟合决策树，挖出人想不到的高损失特征组合）。
why_en: Slices come from business-critical segments named by stakeholders, error-analysis failure patterns, and algorithmic discovery over error residuals.
options: 业务关键 segment：利益相关者点名的高价值群体（付费订阅、高 LTV）
错误分析驱动：把历史反复出现的失败模式转成 slicing function
算法自动发现：如在误差残差上拟合决策树，挖出人忽略的高损失特征组合
随机抽样：每次随机切一批样本当 slice，保证覆盖面
options_en: Business-critical segments: high-value groups named by stakeholders (premium subs, high-LTV).
Error-analysis-driven: turn recurring failure patterns into slicing functions.
Algorithmic discovery: e.g. fit a decision tree on error residuals to surface high-loss feature combos humans miss.
Random sampling: randomly cut a batch each time as a slice to ensure coverage.
optionExplanations: 对；业务点名的高价值群体是必须过关的强制 slice，漏了它等于对最贵的用户失明。
对；错误分析里反复出现的失败模式沉淀成 slicing function，让一次性发现变成长期门禁。
对；算法发现（决策树拟合残差）能挖出人类想不到的高损失特征组合，补人工盲区。
错；随机切片没有语义、不可复现，无法定位失败，也不能当稳定的发布门禁。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — stakeholder-named high-value groups are mandatory slices; missing them blinds you to your costliest users.
Correct — recurring failure patterns from error analysis crystallize into slicing functions, turning one-off findings into standing gates.
Correct — algorithmic discovery (a tree on residuals) surfaces high-loss feature combos humans overlook, covering blind spots.
Incorrect — random slices carry no semantics, aren't reproducible, can't localize failure, and make no stable release gate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户生命周期价值：一个用户预期为产品带来的总收益，高 LTV 群体常是业务关键 slice。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LTV (Lifetime Value) is the expected total revenue a user brings over their lifetime; high-LTV groups are often business-critical slices.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预测与真实值之间的差，算法切片发现常在残差上找高损失区域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An error residual is the gap between prediction and truth; algorithmic slice discovery searches residuals for high-loss regions.

scenario: 你已经列了业务点名和错误分析来的 slice，但担心还有人类没想到的失败子群藏在特征组合里。
scenario_en: You've listed stakeholder and error-analysis slices, but worry about failure subgroups hidden in feature combinations that humans didn't think of.
q: 该用什么方法找出这些人想不到的高损失子群？
q_en: What method surfaces these unanticipated high-loss subgroups?
why: 用算法切片发现：在模型误差残差上拟合一棵决策树，树的分裂会自动圈出高损失的特征组合（如「低 RAM 安卓 + 夜间 + 某类目」）。它补的是人工列 slice 的盲区，发现后再固化成 slicing function。
why_en: Use algorithmic slice discovery: fit a decision tree on error residuals so its splits isolate high-loss feature combinations humans miss.
tradeoff: 算法发现（挖人想不到的组合，但要人复核语义）vs 纯人工列 slice（可解释但有盲区）
whenOtherWins: 如果失败模式已经很清楚、业务点名的高价值 segment 就是关注重点，人工列 slice 更可解释、也够用，不必上算法发现。
options: 把整个评估集再切得更细，穷举所有特征取值的组合
在误差残差上拟合一棵决策树，用它的分裂自动圈出高损失特征组合，再固化成 slicing function
把 aggregate 指标多算几次取平均，方差小了失败自然浮现
直接问业务方还有哪些 segment，人工列举就够了
options_en: Slice the whole eval set even finer, enumerating every feature-value combination.
Fit a decision tree on error residuals so its splits isolate high-loss feature combos, then crystallize them into slicing functions.
Compute the aggregate metric several times and average — lower variance will surface failures on its own.
Just ask the business for more segments; manual enumeration is enough.
optionExplanations: 穷举所有组合会爆炸成海量小样本 slice，噪声大且不可行，不是发现失败的可行路径。
对；决策树在残差上分裂，天然把高损失区域切出来，正是补人工盲区的算法发现方法。
重算均值不产生新信息，均值再准也定位不到隐藏子群，方向错了。
问业务方只能覆盖『人想得到』的 segment，算法发现恰恰是为找到『人想不到』的组合。
optionExplanations_en: Enumerating all combos explodes into countless tiny noisy slices — infeasible, not a way to find failures.
Correct — a tree splitting on residuals naturally carves out high-loss regions, the discovery method that covers human blind spots.
Recomputing the average yields no new info; a sharper average still can't localize hidden subgroups — wrong direction.
Asking the business covers only 'thinkable' segments; algorithmic discovery exists precisely for the 'unthinkable' combos.

termDefinitions.term: algorithmic slice discovery / 算法切片发现
termDefinitions.meaning: 用自动方法（如在残差上拟合决策树）挖出人工没想到的高损失子群。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Algorithmic slice discovery uses automated methods (e.g. a tree on residuals) to surface high-loss subgroups humans didn't anticipate.

scenario: 定义 slice 时，有人想把 slice 切得极细（如「25-26 岁 + 低 RAM 安卓 + 周二夜间 + 某小类目」）以精准定位。
scenario_en: Defining slices, someone wants extremely fine slices (e.g. '25-26yo + low-RAM Android + Tuesday night + one niche category') for precise localization.
q: slice 切得过细会带来什么问题，边界怎么定？
q_en: What's the risk of over-fine slices, and how to set the boundary?
why: 太细 → 样本太小 → 指标估计噪声大，可能在追随机波动；太宽 → 无法隔离失败。原则是：大到能给出可靠估计，小到仍可行动。样本量决定可信度，可行动性决定价值。
why_en: Too fine gives tiny noisy estimates chasing randomness; too broad fails to isolate the failure — aim large enough for reliability, specific enough to act.
tradeoff: 太细（噪声大、追随机）vs 太宽（无法隔离失败）——取『大到可靠、小到可行动』
options: 越细越好，能精确定位到具体人群，样本小不影响结论
太细样本太小、估计噪声大易追随机波动；原则是大到可靠、小到仍可行动
越宽越好，样本大统计最稳，反正能覆盖所有失败
细和宽都无所谓，只要 slice 数量够多就能保证发现问题
options_en: Finer is always better — precise localization, and small samples don't affect the conclusion.
Too fine means tiny samples with noisy estimates chasing randomness; the rule is large enough for reliability, small enough to still act on.
Broader is always better — big samples are most stable and cover all failures anyway.
Fine or broad doesn't matter as long as you have enough slices to guarantee finding problems.
optionExplanations: 样本小恰恰影响结论——50 个样本的 0.70 可能只是噪声，据此行动是浪费。
对；粒度是可靠性和可行动性的权衡，太细追噪声、太宽埋失败，取中间那档。
太宽会把失败子群和健康子群混在一起，均值又把问题盖住，回到了切片要解决的原点。
slice 再多，如果每个都太细全是噪声，也发现不了可信的问题；粒度比数量更关键。
optionExplanations_en: Small samples do affect the conclusion — a 50-sample 0.70 may be noise, and acting on it wastes cycles.
Correct — granularity trades reliability against actionability; too fine chases noise, too broad buries failures, so pick the middle.
Too broad blends failing and healthy subgroups, and the average hides the problem again — back to what slicing was meant to fix.
Even many slices find no trustworthy problem if each is too fine and all noise; granularity matters more than count.

scenario: new_user slice 的 AUC 是 0.62（仅占 8% 流量、样本不多），其余群体都在 0.86 以上，团队提议对 new_user 做 3 倍过采样重训。
scenario_en: The new_user slice shows AUC 0.62 (only 8% traffic, few samples) vs 0.86+ elsewhere; the team proposes 3x oversampling and retraining.
q: 在动手过采样之前，最该先做什么？
q_en: Before oversampling, what should you do first?
why: 先算 95% bootstrap 置信区间：8% 流量、样本少，0.62 可能只是小样本噪声，其区间也许和 0.86 aggregate 重叠。区间证明差距真实再重训，否则 3 倍过采样是在追随机波动、白花训练成本。
why_en: First compute 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, because the small new_user slice's 0.62 may be noise whose interval overlaps the aggregate before you spend a retrain.
tradeoff: 先算 bootstrap CI 确认差距真实 vs 直接过采样（可能在追噪声、浪费重训）
whenOtherWins: 如果 new_user slice 样本量足够大、CI 很窄且明显低于 aggregate，差距已确认真实，那就直接上过采样/切片感知训练。
options: 立刻做 3 倍过采样重训，0.62 明显偏低，越早修越好
先算 new_user slice 的 95% bootstrap 置信区间，确认这 0.62 不是小样本噪声再决定是否重训
把 new_user 直接从评估集删掉，样本少不具代表性
调低分类阈值把 new_user 的 AUC 拉上去
options_en: Immediately do 3x oversampling and retrain — 0.62 is clearly low, the sooner fixed the better.
First compute a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for the new_user slice to confirm the 0.62 isn't small-sample noise before deciding to retrain.
Just drop new_user from the eval set — too few samples to be representative.
Lower the classification threshold to pull new_user's AUC up.
optionExplanations: 8% 流量、样本少时，0.62 很可能带着宽区间，直接重训是在对噪声下重注。
对；bootstrap CI 先判断差距是否统计显著，区间与 aggregate 不重叠再动手，避免追噪声。
删掉 new_user 等于对新用户失明——它可能正是最该保障的业务关键 slice。
调阈值也改不了 AUC（AUC 与阈值无关），且没先确认差距真实就是盲动。
optionExplanations_en: With 8% traffic and few samples, 0.62 likely carries a wide interval, so retraining is a big bet on noise.
Correct — a bootstrap CI first tests whether the gap is statistically significant; act only if the interval doesn't overlap the aggregate.
Dropping new_user blinds you to new users — possibly the very business-critical slice to protect.
Threshold tuning can't change AUC (AUC is threshold-free), and it's blind action without confirming the gap is real.

termDefinitions.term: bootstrap CI / 自助置信区间
termDefinitions.meaning: 对 slice 样本反复有放回重采样估计指标分布，得到该指标的 95% 置信区间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bootstrap CI resamples the slice with replacement to estimate a metric's distribution and its 95% confidence interval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时提高某子群样本的采样比例，让模型更关注该群体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Oversampling raises a subgroup's sampling ratio in training so the model attends to it more.

scenario: 某 slice 指标看起来比 aggregate 低，但它的 95% bootstrap 置信区间和 aggregate 重叠。
scenario_en: A slice metric looks lower than the aggregate, but its 95% bootstrap CI overlaps the aggregate.
q: 置信区间和 aggregate 重叠时该怎么处理？
q_en: When the CI overlaps the aggregate, what should you do?
why: CI 重叠 = 这个差距可能只是噪声，还不构成统计显著。此时标记为『监控观察』而不是立刻干预——对每个看似偏低的小 slice 都重训，是在追随机波动、浪费迭代周期。
why_en: An overlapping CI means the gap may be noise, so flag it for monitoring rather than immediate intervention to avoid chasing randomness.
options: 立刻针对该 slice 重训或改架构，指标偏低就得马上修
标记为『监控观察』而非立即干预——差距可能只是噪声，追它会浪费迭代周期
把该 slice 的阈值直接调低到它当前的水平，让它「达标」
忽略这个 slice，既然重叠就说明它没有任何问题
options_en: Immediately retrain or re-architect for that slice — a low metric must be fixed now.
Flag it for monitoring rather than immediate intervention — the gap may be noise, and chasing it wastes iteration cycles.
Just lower that slice's threshold to its current level so it 'passes'.
Ignore the slice entirely — an overlap means it has no problem at all.
optionExplanations: 重叠说明差距未达统计显著，立刻重训是在对噪声下注，性价比极低。
对；重叠→监控、不重叠→干预，这条规则把有限的迭代资源留给真实退化。
为了『达标』而调低阈值是自欺，等于把门禁标准迁就到问题水平，掩盖而非解决。
重叠只说明『暂不显著』，不等于永远没问题，仍要监控它后续是否走向显著。
optionExplanations_en: Overlap means the gap isn't significant, so retraining now bets on noise — very poor ROI.
Correct — overlap means monitor, non-overlap means intervene; this rule reserves scarce iteration for real degradation.
Lowering the threshold to 'pass' is self-deception — bending the gate to the problem level hides rather than fixes it.
Overlap means 'not significant for now', not 'never a problem'; keep monitoring in case it trends toward significance.

scenario: 欺诈检测里，高价值交易漏一笔损失数千美元，微额交易漏一笔损失很小。团队想给所有 slice 设同一个 recall 阈值。
scenario_en: In fraud detection, missing a high-value transaction costs thousands while missing a micro-transaction costs little; the team wants one recall threshold for all slices.
q: 该给所有 slice 设统一阈值，还是分档？谁来定？
q_en: One threshold for all slices, or tiered, and who sets it?
why: 阈值应按代价分档：高价值交易 recall ≥ 0.95、微额交易 recall ≥ 0.85，因为漏检代价差几个数量级。而且这是业务/政策决策，要和 product/policy 一起定，不是 ML 工程师单方面拍。
why_en: Set asymmetric thresholds by cost — recall ≥ 0.95 on high-value, ≥ 0.85 on micro — and set them with product/policy, not ML engineers alone.
tradeoff: 按代价分档阈值（高价值严、微额松）vs 统一阈值（要么放过高价值风险、要么在微额上过度投入）
whenOtherWins: 如果各 slice 的漏检代价其实差不多、监管也要求一视同仁，统一阈值更简单也更公平，不必分档。
options: 所有 slice 一个统一 recall 阈值，简单一致，由 ML 工程师定就行
按代价分档：高价值交易 recall ≥ 0.95、微额 ≥ 0.85，且和 product/policy 一起定
只给高价值交易设阈值，微额交易不用管
阈值越高越好，所有 slice 都设 recall ≥ 0.99
options_en: One unified recall threshold for all slices — simple and consistent, set by ML engineers.
Tier by cost: recall ≥ 0.95 on high-value, ≥ 0.85 on micro, and set them together with product/policy.
Only set a threshold for high-value transactions; ignore micro-transactions.
Higher is always better — set recall ≥ 0.99 for every slice.
optionExplanations: 统一阈值忽略了几个数量级的代价差：对高价值太松放过风险，对微额太严又过度投入。
对；漏检代价不对称就分档设阈值，且阈值是业务决策，必须拉上 product/policy 共定。
微额也需要一个（较松的）底线，完全不管会让整体风控出现盲区。
全设 0.99 会把 precision 压垮、误拦大量正常交易，代价不对称时是过度反应。
optionExplanations_en: A unified threshold ignores the order-of-magnitude cost gap: too loose lets high-value risk through, too strict over-invests in micro.
Correct — asymmetric miss-cost means tiered thresholds, and thresholds are a business decision co-set with product/policy.
Micro still needs a (looser) floor; ignoring it entirely opens a blind spot in overall risk control.
Setting 0.99 everywhere crushes precision and over-blocks legit transactions — an overreaction under asymmetric cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不同 slice 按各自漏检/误报代价设不同的达标门槛，而非一刀切。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Asymmetric thresholds set different pass bars per slice according to each slice's miss/false-alarm cost rather than one-size-fits-all.

scenario: 欺诈检测按交易价值分档设 recall 阈值，漏检代价随金额相差数量级。
scenario_en: Fraud detection tiers recall thresholds by transaction value, with miss-cost differing by orders of magnitude.
q: 填出按代价分档的 recall 阈值示例：
q_en: Fill in the cost-tiered recall thresholds:
text: 高价值交易（漏一笔损失数千美元）要求 recall ≥ {{0.95}}；微额交易（漏一笔损失很小）要求 recall ≥ {{0.85}}；阈值由 {{product/policy}} 与 ML 一起定，不是工程师单方面拍。
text_en: High-value transactions (a miss costs thousands) require recall ≥ {{0.95}}; micro-transactions (a miss costs little) require recall ≥ {{0.85}}; thresholds are set with {{product/policy}} together with ML, not by engineers alone.
why: 0.95 和 0.85 不是公式算出来的，是按漏检代价定的产品目标：金额相差数量级，达标门槛就该不同。阈值是把「一笔漏检值多少钱」翻译成 recall 底线的业务决策。
why_en: 0.95 and 0.85 aren't computed — they're product targets set by miss-cost, translating 'what a miss costs' into a recall floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某 slice 上线必须达到的最低召回率，按该 slice 漏检代价设定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recall floor is the minimum recall a slice must hit to ship, set by that slice's miss-cost.

scenario: 要给审批会准备一份能跨版本比较、又能逐 slice 看的评估文档。
scenario_en: For an approval meeting you need an eval doc that compares across versions and reads per slice.
q: slice performance matrix 长什么样，为什么用矩阵？
q_en: What does a slice performance matrix look like, and why a matrix?
why: 行 = 模型版本，列 = 各 slice，单元格 = 指标 + 置信区间。矩阵形态让审批会一眼看清「哪个版本在哪个 slice 上退化」，并支持跨版本对比；持续某 slice 落后就该上 slice-aware 训练治根因。
why_en: Rows are model versions, columns are slices, cells are metric plus CI, so the matrix shows at a glance which version regresses on which slice across releases.
options: 一个数字：把所有 slice 指标再平均成一个总分方便汇报
行=模型版本、列=各 slice、单元格=指标+置信区间，支持跨版本逐 slice 对比
一张按时间排的折线图，只看 aggregate 随版本的变化
一份文字报告，逐段描述每个 slice，不做结构化对比
options_en: A single number: average all slice metrics into one score for easy reporting.
Rows = model versions, columns = slices, cells = metric + CI, enabling cross-version per-slice comparison.
A time-series line chart showing only the aggregate across versions.
A prose report describing each slice paragraph by paragraph with no structured comparison.
optionExplanations: 再平均成一个数又回到了 aggregate 淹没 slice 的老问题，矩阵存在的意义就是不合并。
对；版本×slice 的矩阵 + CI 让退化可定位、可跨版本比较，是审批会的中心文档。
只看 aggregate 折线丢掉了 slice 维度，看不出哪个子群在退化。
纯文字不便跨版本对齐比较，矩阵的结构化才支持『这版比上版在这个 slice 差了多少』。
optionExplanations_en: Averaging back to one number returns to aggregate drowning slices — the matrix exists precisely not to merge.
Correct — a version×slice matrix with CIs makes regressions localizable and cross-version comparable, the approval-meeting centerpiece.
An aggregate-only line chart drops the slice dimension and can't show which subgroup regresses.
Prose can't align across versions; the matrix's structure supports 'how much worse is this version on this slice'.

termDefinitions.term: slice performance matrix / 切片表现矩阵
termDefinitions.meaning: 行为模型版本、列为各 slice、格内为指标+置信区间的二维表，用于审批与跨版本对比。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slice performance matrix is a 2D table (versions × slices) with metric+CI cells, used for approval and cross-version comparison.

scenario: 某个业务关键 slice 在连续几个版本里都持续低于阈值，不是偶发噪声。
scenario_en: A business-critical slice persistently underperforms its threshold across several releases — not a one-off fluke.
q: 对持续落后的 slice，该用切片感知训练还是上线后过滤？
q_en: For a persistently lagging slice, slice-aware training or post-hoc filtering?
why: 持续落后说明是根因问题（数据/特征/表征），该上 slice-aware 训练（如对该 slice 加权/过采样/定制特征）从源头修。上线后过滤只是把差结果挡掉、治标，不改模型对该群体的能力。
why_en: Persistent underperformance is a root-cause issue, so use slice-aware training to fix the source rather than post-hoc filtering that only masks bad outputs.
tradeoff: slice-aware 训练（治根因、改模型能力，成本高）vs 上线后过滤（治标、快，但模型能力没变）
whenOtherWins: 如果只是临时救火、等不及重训周期，或该 slice 有明确可后处理的偏差（如已知校准偏移），先用后处理过滤止血也合理。
options: 上线后过滤：在服务端把该 slice 的差结果挡掉，最快最省事
切片感知训练：对该 slice 加权/过采样/定制特征，从数据与表征根因上修
什么都不做，持续落后说明这个 slice 本来就学不好
把该 slice 的阈值调低到它当前水平，让它不再报警
options_en: Post-hoc filtering: block that slice's bad outputs at serving — fastest and easiest.
Slice-aware training: reweight/oversample/custom features for that slice to fix the data and representation root cause.
Do nothing — persistent lag means the slice is just inherently unlearnable.
Lower that slice's threshold to its current level so it stops alerting.
optionExplanations: 过滤只挡住差输出，不提升模型对该群体的能力，根因还在，下版照样落后。
对；持续落后是根因信号，slice-aware 训练从数据/表征上补，才可能真正把该 slice 拉起来。
『本来就学不好』多半是缺信号或缺数据，可通过切片感知训练改善，不该躺平。
调低阈值是掩盖问题，业务关键 slice 的真实体验并没有改善。
optionExplanations_en: Filtering only blocks bad outputs without improving the model's ability on that group; the root cause persists and next release lags again.
Correct — persistent lag signals a root cause, so slice-aware training fixes data/representation to actually lift the slice.
'Inherently unlearnable' usually means missing signal or data, improvable via slice-aware training — don't give up.
Lowering the threshold hides the problem; the business-critical slice's real experience hasn't improved.

termDefinitions.term: slice-aware training / 切片感知训练
termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时针对特定 slice 加权、过采样或加定制特征，从根因提升该子群表现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slice-aware training reweights, oversamples, or adds custom features for a target slice to lift that subgroup from the root cause.

scenario: 要把切片评估从「某次分析」制度化成团队默认流程（Google/Meta 模式）。
scenario_en: You want to institutionalize slice evaluation from a one-off analysis into a team default (Google/Meta pattern).
q: 制度化切片评估的三个组件是哪些？(多选)
q_en: What are the three components of institutionalizing slice evaluation? (multiple)
why: 三件套：① 版本化的 slice registry（切片函数目录，季度 review 随人群演进）；② 自动切片报告（每次训练自动生成 per-slice 报告，附到模型 artifact）；③ CI/CD 里的 slice 回归告警（关键 slice 跌破阈值就阻断发布）。
why_en: A versioned slice registry, automated per-run slice reports attached to the model artifact, and CI/CD slice-regression alerts that block release.
options: 版本化的 slice registry：切片函数目录，与模型代码同存，季度 review
自动切片报告：每次训练自动生成 per-slice 报告，附到模型 artifact
CI/CD 里的 slice 回归告警：关键 slice 跌破阈值就阻断发布
一个每天给全公司群发 aggregate 指标的邮件机器人
options_en: A versioned slice registry: a catalog of slicing functions kept with the model code, reviewed quarterly.
Automated slice reports: every training run auto-generates a per-slice report attached to the model artifact.
CI/CD slice-regression alerts: block release if a critical slice drops below its threshold.
An email bot that blasts the aggregate metric to the whole company daily.
optionExplanations: 对；registry 把切片函数目录化并版本化，季度 review 让它随人群演进而更新。
对；每次训练自动出 per-slice 报告并绑到 artifact，切片评估才不靠人记得跑。
对；CI/CD 门禁把切片阈值升级成可阻断发布的强制闸门，而非仪表盘摆设。
错；群发 aggregate 邮件恰恰是切片评估要取代的『一个数』文化，不解决子群失明。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a registry catalogs and versions slicing functions, with quarterly review keeping them current as populations evolve.
Correct — auto per-slice reports bound to the artifact each run make slice eval not depend on someone remembering to run it.
Correct — a CI/CD gate upgrades slice thresholds into release-blocking enforcement, not a dashboard curiosity.
Incorrect — blasting the aggregate is exactly the 'one number' culture slice eval replaces; it doesn't fix subgroup blindness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 版本化保存所有 slicing function 的目录，与模型代码同管理，定期 review。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slice registry is a version-controlled catalog of all slicing functions managed with the model code and reviewed regularly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续集成/持续交付流水线，可在其中加自动检查作为发布门禁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery) is the automated pipeline where checks can gate releases.

scenario: 新模型 aggregate 指标比线上版本更好，但某个关键 slice 相对当前线上版本掉了几个点。CI/CD 里配了 slice 回归门禁。
scenario_en: A new model beats the serving version on the aggregate, but one critical slice drops a few points versus the currently serving model; a CI/CD slice-regression gate is configured.
q: 配了 slice 回归门禁的意义是什么？
q_en: What's the point of a slice-regression gate?
why: 门禁的意义是可强制执行：任一关键 slice 相对当前线上版本跌破阈值就阻断发布，哪怕 aggregate 更好。这把切片评估从『仪表盘摆设』变成真正拦得住坏版本的闸门——staff 级信号。
why_en: The gate is enforceable: if any critical slice drops below threshold versus the serving model, it blocks release even if the aggregate improved.
options: 只是生成一个好看的仪表盘，最终还是靠人肉决定发不发
可强制执行：任一关键 slice 相对线上版本跌破阈值就阻断发布，即使 aggregate 更好
aggregate 更好就一定放行，slice 门禁只在 aggregate 变差时才触发
门禁只在训练阶段有用，上线决策不受它约束
options_en: It just produces a pretty dashboard; humans still decide whether to ship.
It's enforceable: if any critical slice drops below threshold versus the serving model, it blocks the release even when the aggregate improved.
A better aggregate always passes; the slice gate triggers only when the aggregate worsens.
The gate only matters during training and doesn't constrain the release decision.
optionExplanations: 仪表盘不阻断发布就没有约束力，坏版本照样能上；门禁的价值恰在于强制拦截。
对；aggregate 更好但关键 slice 退化就该拦，门禁把 per-slice 阈值变成硬约束。
恰恰相反——门禁就是为了在 aggregate 变好、slice 却退化时也能拦住，避免被均值骗过。
门禁作用在发布环节（CI/CD），正是约束上线决策，不只训练阶段。
optionExplanations_en: A dashboard that doesn't block ships has no teeth; bad versions still go out — the gate's value is enforced interception.
Correct — a better aggregate with a critical-slice regression should be blocked; the gate makes per-slice thresholds hard constraints.
Quite the opposite — the gate exists to block precisely when the aggregate improves but a slice regresses, so the average can't fool you.
The gate acts at release (CI/CD), constraining the ship decision, not only training.

q: 把一条完整的切片评估流水线排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order a complete slice-evaluation pipeline correctly:
steps: 把关键 slice 的阈值配成 CI/CD 发布门禁，跌破就阻断上线
定义 slicing function（业务/错误分析/算法发现三来源）
用 slicing function 切分评估集，逐 slice 算指标 + bootstrap 置信区间
把切片函数与报告制度化进版本化 registry，每次训练自动生成
why: 顺序：定义 slicing function → 切分并逐 slice 算指标+CI → 把阈值配成发布门禁 → 制度化进 registry 自动跑。前三步是单次评估，第四步把它变成团队默认流程。
why_en: Define slicing functions, partition and compute per-slice metrics with CIs, wire thresholds into release gates, then institutionalize into a registry that runs automatically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  D["定义 slicing fn"] --> C["切分+逐slice指标+CI"]
  C --> G["阈值→发布门禁"]
  G --> R["制度化进 registry"]

scenario: 面试做 YouTube 推荐或 Uber ETA 的评估设计，你想给出资深级别的答案。
scenario_en: Designing evaluation for YouTube recs or Uber ETA in an interview, you want a staff-level answer.
q: 在评估设计里提什么，最能传递 staff 级思维？
q_en: What proposal best signals staff-level thinking in evaluation design?
why: 提出 slice registry + per-slice 发布门禁，传递的核心判断是：ML 服务的是异质人群，一个 aggregate 数字不够。把子群验收前置成可强制的门禁，正是 staff 级看待评估的方式。
why_en: Proposing a slice registry plus per-slice release gates signals the staff insight that ML serves heterogeneous populations, so one aggregate number is insufficient.
options: 强调把 aggregate 指标做到行业最高，其余交给上线后监控
提出 slice registry + per-slice 发布门禁，点明 ML 服务异质人群、单个 aggregate 不够
承诺用最大的模型，靠容量把所有 slice 一起拉高
只说会做 A/B 测试，用线上指标代替离线切片评估
options_en: Emphasize pushing the aggregate metric to industry-best and leave the rest to post-launch monitoring.
Propose a slice registry plus per-slice release gates, noting ML serves heterogeneous populations so one aggregate isn't enough.
Promise the biggest model and lift all slices together via capacity.
Just say you'll run A/B tests, using online metrics instead of offline slice evaluation.
optionExplanations: 只追 aggregate 最高正是被均值蒙蔽的做法，恰恰缺了子群视角。
对；registry + 门禁体现『异质人群 + 前置强制验收』的判断，是资深评估观。
堆容量不保证每个 slice 都提升，冷启动/长尾等子群可能对容量不敏感。
A/B 是上线后验证，替代不了离线切片评估在发布前拦住子群退化的作用。
optionExplanations_en: Chasing only the aggregate is exactly the average-blinded approach, missing the subgroup lens.
Correct — registry plus gates embodies 'heterogeneous populations plus front-loaded enforcement', a senior evaluation stance.
Piling on capacity doesn't guarantee every slice improves; cold-start/long-tail subgroups may be capacity-insensitive.
A/B is post-launch validation and can't replace offline slice eval catching subgroup regressions before release.

scenario: 同事说「aggregate 指标已经够了，切片评估是过度工程」。
scenario_en: A colleague says 'aggregate metrics are enough; slice evaluation is over-engineering.'
q: aggregate 指标和切片评估的关系该怎么表述？
q_en: How should you frame aggregate metrics versus slice evaluation?
why: aggregate 是必要但不充分：它给整体健康度的快速信号，但会数学上淹没少数群体退化。切片评估在它之上按运营子集（地区/设备/类别/时段）分解，二者互补而非替代。
why_en: Aggregate metrics are necessary but insufficient — they give a fast overall signal yet drown minority degradation, which slice evaluation decomposes.
tradeoff: aggregate（快、整体健康度，但淹没少数群体）vs 切片（暴露子群退化，但更重、要维护）
options: 切片评估可以完全取代 aggregate，以后只看矩阵不看总分
aggregate 必要但不充分：给整体快速信号却淹没少数群体，切片在其上分解，二者互补
aggregate 就够了，切片只是锦上添花，可有可无
两者冲突，只能二选一，选了切片就不该再看 aggregate
options_en: Slice evaluation fully replaces the aggregate — from now on only read the matrix, never the total.
Aggregate is necessary but insufficient: a fast overall signal that drowns minorities, and slice evaluation decomposes on top — complementary.
The aggregate is enough; slicing is a nice-to-have, entirely optional.
They conflict, so pick one — choosing slices means never looking at the aggregate again.
optionExplanations: 完全取代过头了：aggregate 仍是整体健康度的快速信号，切片是在它之上补维度。
对；『必要但不充分』一句点清关系——aggregate 打底、切片补子群，互补共用。
『可有可无』低估了子群失明的代价，Airbnb 0.51 的案例就是反例。
两者不冲突，是分工：aggregate 看整体、切片看子群，一起用信息最全。
optionExplanations_en: Full replacement overshoots: the aggregate is still a fast overall-health signal, and slices add dimensions on top.
Correct — 'necessary but insufficient' nails it: aggregate as baseline, slices for subgroups, used together.
'Optional' underestimates the cost of subgroup blindness — the Airbnb 0.51 case is the counterexample.
They don't conflict; it's a division of labor: aggregate for the whole, slices for subgroups, most informative together.

scenario: 广告排序系统里，低 RAM 安卓机上因延迟预算紧、推理时会截断部分计算，怀疑这类设备预测更差。
scenario_en: In ads ranking, low-RAM Android devices truncate some inference under a tight latency budget; you suspect worse predictions there.
q: 该定义什么 slicing function 来验证这个怀疑？
q_en: What slicing function verifies this suspicion?
why: 定义设备类型 slice：device = low_RAM_Android，单独算它的指标。这类设备因延迟限制在推理时截断计算，天然可能预测更差，是设备维度的典型 slice；切出来才看得见 aggregate 里被盖住的退化。
why_en: Define a device slice like device = low_RAM_Android and compute its metrics, since latency-truncated inference on such devices plausibly degrades predictions.
tradeoff: 按设备切片（暴露低端机的延迟截断退化）vs 只看整体（被高端机流量盖住）
whenOtherWins: 如果延迟预算对所有设备一致、不存在按设备的推理截断差异，设备切片就区分不出问题，该换到更相关的维度（地区/类目）。
options: 按用户年龄切片，因为年龄决定点击习惯
定义 device = low_RAM_Android 的设备 slice，单独算这类设备的指标
把所有设备合并成一个 slice，反正都是移动端
按广告主 id 切成上千个微 slice，逐个看
options_en: Slice by user age, since age drives click habits.
Define a device slice device = low_RAM_Android and compute metrics for these devices alone.
Merge all devices into one slice — they're all mobile anyway.
Slice by advertiser id into thousands of micro-slices and inspect each.
optionExplanations: 年龄和『延迟截断导致预测差』没有直接因果，切它验证不了这个具体怀疑。
对；怀疑源于低 RAM 安卓的推理截断，就该按这个设备维度切片，直接对准假设。
合并所有设备正好把低端机的退化混进高端机流量里盖住，回到 aggregate 失明。
按广告主切成上千微 slice 会小样本噪声爆炸，且偏离『设备延迟截断』这个假设。
optionExplanations_en: Age has no direct causal link to 'latency-truncation degradation', so slicing it can't verify this specific suspicion.
Correct — the suspicion is low-RAM-Android inference truncation, so slice on that device dimension to target the hypothesis.
Merging all devices blends low-end degradation into high-end traffic and hides it — back to aggregate blindness.
Slicing by advertiser into thousands of micro-slices explodes small-sample noise and strays from the device-truncation hypothesis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为满足延迟预算，在低端设备推理时截断部分特征或计算，可能降低预测质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Latency truncation cuts some features or computation during inference on low-end devices to meet a latency budget, potentially hurting prediction quality.

scenario: 要落地切片评估，团队问有没有现成工具而不是全自己写。
scenario_en: To implement slice evaluation, the team asks for existing tooling rather than building from scratch.
q: 文中点名了哪些切片评估相关工具？
q_en: Which slice-evaluation tools does the lesson name?
why: Snorkel Slicing Functions（写和管理切片函数）和 TFMA（TensorFlow Model Analysis，按 slice 批量算指标）。用现成工具能把切片函数版本化、自动出 per-slice 报告，少造轮子。
why_en: Snorkel Slicing Functions for authoring/managing slices and TFMA for computing per-slice metrics at scale.
options: Kafka 和 Flink，用来做流式切片
Snorkel Slicing Functions 和 TFMA（TensorFlow Model Analysis）
Airflow 和 Spark，专门用来切片
Redis 和 DynamoDB，用来存切片结果
options_en: Kafka and Flink, for streaming slices.
Snorkel Slicing Functions and TFMA (TensorFlow Model Analysis).
Airflow and Spark, dedicated to slicing.
Redis and DynamoDB, to store slice results.
optionExplanations: Kafka/Flink 是流处理设施，不是切片评估工具，用来算 per-slice 指标不对口。
对；Snorkel 管切片函数、TFMA 按 slice 批量出指标，是文中点名的两件工具。
Airflow/Spark 是编排与批处理，可承载切片计算，但不是文中点名的切片评估专用工具。
Redis/DynamoDB 是低延迟存储，和切片评估的指标计算没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka/Flink are stream-processing infra, not slice-eval tools; ill-suited to computing per-slice metrics.
Correct — Snorkel manages slicing functions and TFMA computes per-slice metrics at scale, the two tools named.
Airflow/Spark are orchestration/batch that can host slice compute but aren't the named slice-eval tools.
Redis/DynamoDB are low-latency stores, unrelated to slice-eval metric computation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 谷歌的模型分析库，能按 slice 批量计算并可视化评估指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TFMA (TensorFlow Model Analysis) is Google's library for computing and visualizing evaluation metrics per slice at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: Snorkel 框架里用来声明式定义和管理评估切片的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Snorkel Slicing Functions is the Snorkel component for declaratively defining and managing evaluation slices.

scenario: slice registry 建好后放着不管，一年后用户结构和内容生态已经和当初大不相同。
scenario_en: The slice registry is built then left untouched; a year later the user base and content ecosystem look very different.
q: 为什么 slice registry 要定期（季度）review？
q_en: Why should the slice registry be reviewed regularly (quarterly)?
why: 人群和产品在演进：新市场、新设备、新内容类目不断出现，旧 slice 会漏掉新兴的高风险子群。季度 review 让切片目录跟上人群变化，否则门禁守的是过时的地图。
why_en: Populations and products evolve, so the registry needs periodic review or its slices go stale and miss newly emerging high-risk subgroups.
options: 为了删掉旧 slice 节省存储，切片越少跑得越快
人群与产品在演进，旧 slice 会漏掉新兴高风险子群，review 让目录跟上变化
为了每季度换一批全新 slice，制造工作量证明团队在忙
registry 一旦建好就不该改，review 只是形式
options_en: To delete old slices and save storage — fewer slices run faster.
Populations and products evolve, so stale slices miss newly emerging high-risk subgroups; review keeps the catalog current.
To swap in a fully new batch each quarter to generate busywork proving the team is busy.
Once built the registry shouldn't change — review is just a formality.
optionExplanations: review 的目的不是省存储——切片数量不是瓶颈，漏掉新兴风险子群才是真代价。
对；新市场/设备/类目会带来新的高风险子群，季度 review 让切片目录不落后于人群演进。
不是为凑工作量换新 slice，而是按人群实际变化增删，保持目录与现实对齐。
registry 恰恰需要随人群演进而更新，一成不变会让门禁守着过时地图。
optionExplanations_en: Review isn't about saving storage — slice count isn't the bottleneck; missing emerging risk subgroups is the real cost.
Correct — new markets/devices/categories bring new high-risk subgroups, and quarterly review keeps the catalog abreast of population drift.
Not busywork swapping — you add/remove per actual population change to keep the catalog aligned with reality.
The registry must evolve with the population; static slices leave the gate guarding a stale map.
